informal_statement: If something is necessarily true, then its necessity leads to a contradiction.
informal_proof:
Assume that we have a statement $\phi$ that is necessarily true, denoted by $\Box\phi$. In intuitionistic logic, if $\Box\phi$ is true, it implies that $\phi$ must hold in all possible worlds or scenarios.

Now, suppose we have $\Box\phi \vdash \bot$, which means assuming $\Box\phi$ leads to a contradiction ($\bot$). This suggests that the assumption of $\phi$ being necessarily true is incompatible with the rules of intuitionistic logic, causing a contradiction to arise.

Intuitionistically, necessity is closely tied to the verification or proof of a statement across all possible contexts. If $\Box\phi$ holds, then by definition, $\phi$ is such that it is always verifiable, leaving no room for contradiction unless the system itself is inconsistent.

The proof leverages logical equivalences and axioms to show that assuming $\Box\phi$ leads to an unavoidable contradiction, thereby demonstrating that such an assumption is inherently flawed within the framework of intuitionistic logic.

def bot_of_dia : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ➝ ⊥ := by
  /-
    S : Type u_1
    F : Type u_2
    inst✝³ : LO.BasicModalLogicalConnective F
    inst✝² : DecidableEq F
    inst✝¹ : LO.System F S
    𝓢 : S
    inst✝ : LO.System.Ver 𝓢
    φ : F
    ⊢ LO.System.Prf 𝓢 (LO.Arrow.arrow (LO.Dia.dia φ) Bot.bot)
  -/
  have : 𝓢 ⊢ ∼◇φ ➝ (◇φ ➝ ⊥) := and₁' $ neg_equiv (𝓢 := 𝓢) (φ := ◇φ);
  exact this ⨀ (contra₀' (and₁' diaDuality) ⨀ by
    apply dni';
    apply axiomVer;
  );
